lawRefs: N.J.S.A. 54A:6-10 and 54A:6-15 (pension and other retirement income exclusions)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed from the fetched source documents; sha256 (when filled) is of the canonical body. Brackets (Table A: single, MFS; Table B: MFJ, HOH, surviving spouse) and exemptions are from the 2026 Form NJ-1040-ES instructions; the pension exclusion chart is from the NJ-1040 resident return instructions (line 28a); cross-checked against Tax Foundation 2026. New Jersey does not start from federal AGI or federal taxable income: it taxes its own categories of gross income (losses in one category do not offset another, there are no federal-style deductions, and most federal above-the-line adjustments are not allowed). startingPoint is set to federalAGI as the closest approximation. There is no standard deduction. personalExemption is $1,000 per filer/spouse; age 65+ adds $1,000 each (seniorExtraDeduction); blind/disabled adds $1,000; veterans add $6,000; dependents $1,500 each (+$1,000 for a full-time college student under 22). Social Security is not taxed. Retirement income exclusion (age 62+ or disabled): maximum $100,000 MFJ, $75,000 single/HOH/surviving spouse, $50,000 MFS when total income is $100,000 or less; for total income $100,001-$125,000 it is 50% (MFJ) / 37.5% (single, HOH) / 25% (MFS) of pension income; for $125,001-$150,000 it is 25% / 18.75% / 12.5%; there is NO exclusion above $150,000 total income. On a joint return only the income of a spouse who is 62+ can be excluded. amountPerPerson holds the single-filer maximum; the MFJ maximum is $100,000 for the couple, not 2 x $75,000. Not modeled: property tax deduction/credit, medical expenses over 2% of income, credit for taxes paid to other jurisdictions. Brackets are not indexed.

flags.retirementIncomeExclusion: simplified: $75,000 is the single maximum; MFJ cap is $100,000 per couple ($50,000 MFS); exclusion is reduced above $100,000 total income and is ZERO above $150,000 total income (cliff not expressible)
flags.startingPoint: NJ uses its own gross-income base, not federal AGI
